question: The salary of an employee in the month of March is ₹7,500 and the company increases his salary every month by 2%. His salary in the month of May of the same year is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The time duration from March to May is 2 months (March → April, April → May).

Effective percentage increase for 2 successive months = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Effective increase = 2 + 2 + (2 × 2) ÷ 100 = 4.04%

Salary in May = Initial Salary × (100% + 4.04%)

Salary in May = 7500 × 1.0404 = 7803

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,803.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/206c1757605560c587c79821a01d82c648d09caa26849b3e9add8c296c8c3299.png] 

**Given:**

Initial salary in March = ₹7,500

Monthly rate of increment (R) = 2%

Number of increments (T) = 2 months

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + R ÷ 100)T

**Calculations:**

⇒ Salary in May = 7500 × (1 + 2 ÷ 100)²

⇒ Salary in May = 7500 × (102 ÷ 100) × (102 ÷ 100)

⇒ Salary in May = 7500 × 1.02 × 1.02

⇒ Salary in May = 7500 × 1.0404

⇒ Salary in May = 7803

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,803.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

When a value is sequentially increased by a% and then by b%, the effective percentage change is given by: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest Analogy

A consistent percentage increase over uniform time periods directly works on the principle of compound interest: A = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ, where the base updates after each period.

Multiplying Factor Approach

An increase of r% corresponds to multiplying the initial value by a factor of (1 + r ÷ 100). For successive increases, simply multiply these factors together.
